solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Long path's edging drawn with stern authority

indicators.note: drawn as in drawn back, so the word for edging is pulled round to read the other way

parts.note: a lip is the edging of a cup or a crater
stern and grim both describe a severe look
to hold sway is to have authority

explanation.surface: A long path's border drawn by some strict figure in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' means drawn back. The Pilgrims' Way is an ancient route in southern England to Canterbury; the apostrophe may go before or after the S, or be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pilgrims' Way is a long-distance historic trackway walked by medieval pilgrims to Canterbury.

clue.text: United's latest goalkeeper?

definitions.note: joined together as a single unit

parts.note: the latest fashion is what is in
a football goalkeeper traditionally wears the number one shirt

explanation.surface: A question about the newest keeper signed by a football club called United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like the football club, but it is the definition; the goalkeeper is the shirt number he wears.
explanation.definitionFit: Things joined together are combined into a single whole, so united.

clue.text: In delight, soldier finds Scottish location

indicators.note: the soldier is placed in the word for delight

parts.note: glee is joyful delight
NCO, a non-commissioned officer, is a soldier such as a sergeant

explanation.surface: A happy soldier comes upon a spot in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Glencoe is a glen in the Scottish Highlands, known for the 1692 massacre.
explanation.definitionFit: Glencoe is a valley and village in the Highlands of Scotland, so a place there.

clue.text: Energetic Nicoise revolutionary embracing drive

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
the two clue words hold the letters within them, embracing them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lively, rebellious person from Nice taking up some cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'embracing drive' as the definition, but 'embracing' signals the hidden letters, so only 'drive' defines. 'revolutionary' turns ETICNI round.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone to act is to urge or provoke them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Panda's injury mark covering large muscle

indicators.note: the mark goes around the muscle, covering it

parts.note: a scar is the mark an injury leaves
the quad, short for quadriceps, is the large thigh muscle

explanation.surface: A panda's scar sits over its big thigh muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panda' is not the animal: a panda car was the British name for a small police patrol car, once painted in blue and white.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panda car was the British nickname for a police patrol vehicle, a type of police car.

clue.text: Dad's holding up fizzy Cola drink

indicators.note: in a down answer, Dad sits underneath the other piece, holding it up
fizzy suggests the letters bubbling into a new order

parts.note: pop is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: Father is holding up a fizzy cola drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcopop is a sweet fizzy alcoholic beverage sold ready-mixed in bottles.

clue.text: He's abroad and on peak, carrying through dream to crack what's unknown?

definitions.text: He's abroad and on peak, carrying through dream to crack what's unknown?

indicators.note: the anagram holds the other pieces inside it, carrying them
to crack the word dream is to break it up and rearrange it
in a down answer one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: und is German for and, so and as said abroad
a hill is a small peak
y is a mathematical unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A mountaineer abroad, on a summit, fulfilling his dream of conquering the unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to crack' scrambles the dream, whose letters split to go round the German and the hill. Only partly all-in-one: 'He's' and 'through' just link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edmund Hillary, the New Zealander who made the first ascent of Everest with Tenzing Norgay, fits a man on a peak achieving a dream.

clue.text: Heather needs posh car when taking out male dish in Milan?

parts.note: ling is a name for common heather
U means upper-class, so posh

indicators.note: the male letter is taken out of the word for the car

parts.note: the Mini is a small car

explanation.surface: Someone wants heather and a smart car, minus a man, for an Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking out' removes M from MINI, leaving INI.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguini is a flat ribbon pasta, a typical plate of food in an Italian city.

clue.text: Ancient writer, close to ninety, brought in pedestal and reeled about

indicators.note: the letter is brought into the word for pedestal

parts.note: a plinth is the pedestal under a statue

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter
about signals the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: An old author near ninety, set on a pedestal, staggered around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to ninety' is Y, which goes into PLINTH; 'about' rearranges REELED as EELDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliny the Elder was a Roman author of the first century, famous for his Natural History.

clue.text: Crowd start to rally in a symbol of peace

indicators.note: the letter is placed in the bird

parts.note: the dove is a traditional symbol of peace

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A crowd begins rallying around a peace emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a large moving mass of people or animals, a near synonym of a throng.

clue.text: Former statesman's dismay following rogue casing hotel

indicators.note: the word for dismay comes after the other piece
the rogue holds the letter inside it, like a case

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible rogue
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to chill someone is to dismay or dispirit them

explanation.surface: A former politician dismayed after a scoundrel surrounds a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill was the British wartime prime minister, a statesman of the past.

clue.text: Impassive old Conservative admitted to joint

indicators.note: the pieces are let into the word for joint

parts.note: united means joint or combined
ex means former or old

explanation.surface: A deadpan former Tory let into a shared venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing no emotion or stir, someone impassive is calm and unmoved.

clue.text: One-time designer of software avoiding type of driver

indicators.note: the letter is avoided, so left out of the word

parts.note: a plugin is a piece of add-on software
L stands for a learner driver, from the L-plates they display

explanation.surface: A former software designer who steers clear of a particular driver program.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type of driver' suggests a computer device driver, but it is a learner, L, as on British L-plates. A.W.N. Pugin designed the interiors of the Houses of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus Pugin was a nineteenth-century Gothic Revival architect, so a designer from the past.

clue.text: Times editor leading with the same as the i?

definitions.note: describing the condition of a small letter i, which carries a dot

indicators.note: the word for the same comes first, leading the other pieces

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same
T is the abbreviation for time, so two of them make times

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor heads a paper the same as the i, another British daily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' and 'the i' look like British newspapers. Here Times is two Ts and the i is just the letter, which has a dot.
explanation.definitionFit: A lower-case letter i carries a point above it, so it is marked with a dot.

clue.text: Least confident bird bypassing mass on certain days of the year

indicators.note: the bird goes round the other pieces, passing by them on both sides

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
the Ides were fixed days in the Roman calendar, such as 15 March

explanation.surface: The shyest bird skips Mass on particular days of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the most timid means having the least confidence, a superlative synonym.

clue.text: Crooked pair entering need to get cosmetics

indicators.note: the reworked letters enter the word for need

parts.note: want means need or lack

indicators.note: crooked suggests the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A shady couple, desperate for money, go after make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: War paint is a jocular term for heavy make-up, from the face paint of warriors.

clue.text: Settle for discussion in which place? Oxford maybe

parts.note: to foot a bill is to settle it

indicators.note: things for discussion are spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: where asks in which place

explanation.surface: A debate over where to settle, with Oxford University as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the university city, but an oxford is a lace-up shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxford is a style of laced leather shoe, an example of things worn on the feet.

clue.text: Popular? I'm surprised work's given to me!

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
my is an exclamation of surprise
a book is a literary work

explanation.surface: A writer is astonished that a popular book has been passed on to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in my opinion, so as far as I am concerned.

clue.text: Remote country home in competition for fuel

indicators.note: the pieces go in the word for competition

parts.note: a bee is a contest, as in a spelling bee
NZ, New Zealand, is a country remote from Britain
in means at home

explanation.surface: A faraway nation hosting a contest to win fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Benzine is a petroleum distillate used as a solvent and motor spirit, a kind of fuel.

clue.text: Meal that's appreciated by Jack and fiancée on a regular basis

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you, said when help is appreciated
J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every second one

explanation.surface: A dinner that a man called Jack and his fiancée regularly enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a regular basis' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of fiancée, INE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tajine is a slow-cooked North African stew, named after the clay pot it is cooked in.

clue.text: Referee's essentially hard on one using teeth

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits on top of the next
the essence of a word is its middle, so its central letters

parts.note: a biter is someone who uses their teeth

explanation.surface: A tough referee is in essence somebody who bites.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter judges disputes, so a synonym for a referee or umpire.

clue.text: In the saddle, senior community separately returned to hunt

indicators.note: each piece is turned round on its own rather than all together

parts.note: EU, European Union, once the European Community
up means riding, in the saddle

explanation.surface: A senior figure on horseback, with the local community, heads back to the hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separately returned' turns each of the three short pieces round on its own, not the whole string at once.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue is to chase after, which is what hunting means as a verb.

clue.text: The French academic's deceived

parts.note: le is French for the
a don is a university academic

explanation.surface: The French scholar has been tricked.
explanation.definitionFit: To be strung along or misled by false promises is to be deceived.

clue.text: Particular sketch intensively read by Brad, say

parts.note: to thumb a book is to read it so much its pages get worn
a brad is a small thin nail, so an example of a nail

explanation.surface: A man named Brad pores over a specific drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brad' looks like a man's name, but a brad is a slim headless nail.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail sketch is a brief, small drawing or description, a specific kind of sketch.

clue.text: With son moving last, stand up for star group

indicators.note: the son's letter moves to the end of the word

parts.note: to arise is to stand up

explanation.surface: A son moves to the back and stands up for a band of stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is a constellation and a zodiac sign, a named cluster of stars.

clue.text: News updates about corrupt iTunes being out of date?

indicators.note: the feed letters go about, round, the other piece

parts.note: RSS feeds deliver news updates on the web

indicators.note: corrupt files are scrambled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: News feeds report on a corrupted iTunes app being obsolete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' scrambles the app's name and 'about' puts the feed letters round it. The definition is playful: an old, unused thing goes rusty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old and neglected goes rusty, so rustiness playfully suggests a state of being outdated.

clue.text: Second staple put on back of carpet

indicators.note: the staple is placed on after the other letter
the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: A second staple fixed onto the back of a carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staple' looks like a fixing, but it is a staple food. 'Second' means a moment, as in 'in a trice'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trice is a very short moment, so a second in the casual sense of an instant.

clue.text: Laurel and Hardy character might get this

definitions.text: Laurel and Hardy character might get this

parts.words: Laurel and Hardy character might get this
parts.note: a laurel is an honour, and someone of hardy, brave character might be awarded this gallantry medal

explanation.walkthrough: The comedy duo is a decoy: read 'Laurel' as an honour and 'Hardy character' as a brave person.
explanation.definitionFit: The George Cross is the highest British civilian award for gallantry, given to the conspicuously brave.
